notes: Color tonal ramps are synthesized OKLCH display metadata, not additional implemented theme tokens. Their eight values keep the source hue/chroma and vary lightness; browser gamut mapping may apply.
Component snippets reproduce visual structure and CSS states without the application runtime. Static stepper previews do not change the output.
Live CSS variables bind the previews to existing root tokens; other source colors remain literal values.
Bundled Nunito Sans fonts are registered under the CSS family name Nunito.

Names remain internal: the picker shows images only with generic accessible labels Аватар N. Додати гравця opens Обери аватар with the instruction Обери картинку для гравця. Ім’я введи в команді. Choosing an avatar creates a player with an empty name for manual entry. The clickable player-row portrait opens the picker titled Змінити аватар; there is no separate text action. Its native button has a player/team-specific accessible label. Replacement changes only the portrait, preserving the player name. Existing saved names and selections remain intact. Closing returns focus to the opener if connected.

Image-only avatar options use two equal grid columns, with twenty-five entries occupying thirteen rows and one choice in the last row, 12px gaps and 8px 0 12px container padding. Buttons have a 1px #d4d3c0 border, #fffaf0 background, 12px corners, 12px 8px padding. Buttons contain the portrait only, without visible catalog-name labels. Hover is #e5ebdc with a 0.16s background transition. Choices are immediate actions, not pressed-state toggles. The native dialog scrolls within its existing height cap to reach the final choice on small screens.

Portrait CSS sizes: player-row portrait and native button target 56px × 56px; avatar dialog 112px × 128px with max-width 100%; word entry 88px × 96px; playing 72px × 80px; handoffs, privacy cover and turn summary 160px × 176px. Team scoreboard and final-results rows use names and scores without images. The hat and victory rasters remain in public/art/; all twenty-five character rasters (twenty-three photo-based and two fictional) are in data/persons/img/. All twenty-seven shipping rasters have provenance sidecars.

New teams start empty with a zero-player count and muted 14px message. Players can be added and removed manually; advancing requires at least two named players per team. Team naming combines an editable custom text field with a native 48px-minimum select using data/teams.ts suggestions; the select has an explicit 16px font size after font:inherit, 10px padding, 1px #d4d3c0 border, 12px corners and #fffaf0 background.

At the user’s explicit request, the mobile viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no, viewport-fit=cover. html, body and dialog use touch-action:pan-x pan-y to permit panning without pinch zoom; buttons retain touch-action:manipulation under those ancestor restrictions. Player-name and word inputs use explicit 16px text; the team preset select sets font-size:16px after font:inherit. Team-name input text remains 19px. Ordinary scrolling, dialog scrolling, safe-area layout and keyboard focus remain available. Browser accessibility overrides may still permit zoom; no real-phone verification is claimed.

narrative.overview:
Cream paper, forest-green actions, warm accents and gouache artwork make the shared phone feel like a small tabletop game. The illustrated hat and player-owned cat portraits, combining photo-based people with fictional base avatars, supply character; rounded controls and quiet paper surfaces keep the interface welcoming and readable.

The system stays compact and centered, even on desktop. Headings, the current player, a visible countdown and one clearly drawn word slip carry the game. Private handoffs and pauses replace the word with a calm confirmation screen, while Ukrainian copy addresses the player directly.
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper with forest-green ink and actions.
Gouache hat, trophy and player-owned cat portraits.
Comfortaa headings paired with self-hosted Nunito Sans body text.
Large rounded touch controls and restrained tactile depth.
A centered mobile column with private handoffs and visible timer feedback.

rules.name: The Action Color Rule
rules.body: Green advances or confirms; soft coral identifies skipping; yellow marks round guidance and winners. Keep the labels and symbols that explain those roles.

rules.name: The Readable Word Rule
rules.body: Keep the active word in Comfortaa, centered on its paper slip, with wrapping for long words and phrases. Animation never delays its visibility.

rules.name: The Shared Phone Rule
rules.body: Prioritize the current player, private content and the next action inside the centered column; retain explicit handoff screens before revealing private words.

dos: **Do** retain cream paper, forest-green actions, soft coral skips and butter-yellow guidance.
**Do** use the existing local gouache hat and trophy, and attach an approved catalog cat portrait to each player rather than to their team.
**Do** pair Comfortaa headings with the shipped Nunito Sans fonts and visible, wrapping Ukrainian labels.
**Do** preserve 48px touch controls, the warm keyboard focus outline and reduced-motion behavior.
**Do** keep the active word visible immediately, with round-specific instruction and visible countdown feedback.
**Do** hide private words behind handoff, privacy-cover and pause screens.
donts: **Don't** substitute emoji, glyph icons or generic stock illustrations for the shipped SVG controls and gouache artwork.
**Don't** depend on color or sound alone to explain actions, scoring or time remaining.
**Don't** replace the centered mobile game flow with a dense desktop dashboard.
**Don't** expose private words on handoff or pause screens, or animate their appearance after a delay.
**Don't** expand the control shadows into a general hard-shadow decoration system.
